name: Reverse Hill-Sachs Lesion
definition: Impaction defect of the anteromedial humeral head produced during posterior shoulder dislocation.

investigations.principle: CT quantifies humeral-head defect; MRI assesses associated labral/soft-tissue injury.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, labral, tendon, cartilage, ligament or occult injury assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

green: Rehabilitation after stable reduction in selected small lesions
amber: Large defects or recurrent instability may need reconstructive surgery.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Amsa/Asthi-Sandhi traumatic phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Impaction defect of the anteromedial humeral head produced during posterior shoulder dislocation.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, unreduced dislocation, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected tendon rupture, infection or other listed red flags.
